title: OpenIAP Commerce Protocol store facts
description:
What each store's own commerce surface offers. A capability descriptor's `provider` axis answers the same question and MUST agree with this document; the descriptor keeps its `implementation` axis, which only that backend can answer.

These are observations of vendor documentation at a point in time, not obligations on the vendor, so a consumer MUST treat an absent store or capability as unknown rather than as absent-from-the-store.

specVersion.description: OpenIAP Commerce Protocol version this table was written against, as MAJOR.MINOR.

stores.description: Keyed by store, using the same open value space as the event envelope. A table lists only the stores this version has examined.

StoreFact.description: One store's commerce surface, capability by capability. The axis names match the capability descriptor's, so a reader can put the two documents side by side. The container stays open, so a consumer ignores an axis it does not recognise; every axis named here is required, so adding one obliges this specification to answer it for every store it lists.

initialValidation.description: Server-side receipt or token validation on demand.

serverNotifications.description: The store pushes lifecycle notifications to a backend.

subscriptions.description: The store exposes a subscription resource a canonical record can be built from.

renewalEvents.description: Renewal is reported as a distinct lifecycle signal.

refundEvents.description: Refund or revocation of a subscription is reported as a distinct lifecycle signal.

expiration.description: Expiry is reported, rather than only inferred from a timestamp having passed.

reconciliation.description: An authoritative endpoint can be re-read on a schedule, so a lost notification can be repaired.

entitlements.description: Current entitlement is answerable for access gating.

revenueAmount.description: The store asserts an amount that can be attributed to revenue with `store` provenance.

FactDelivery.description: How a store makes a capability reachable. This is the detail a boolean cannot carry, and the reason two stores that both answer "yes" can still need different integrations: one store pushes an amount on the notification, another returns it from a follow-up read, a third publishes it only in a periodic export. A surface is a server-reachable API; a report a human downloads from a vendor console is not one, and belongs in `notes` under an `available: false`. Where more than one surface offers the fact, `delivery` and `surface` name the most immediate: push before pull before batch.

Fact.description: One store's answer for one capability. `available` is the value a capability descriptor's `provider` axis copies; `delivery` and `surface` carry the shape that boolean cannot.

available.description: Whether the store offers this at all. A fact about the store, independent of any backend. False means no documented surface exists, which is a far stronger statement than "no backend has built it".

delivery.description: How the store makes it reachable. `none` exactly when `available` is false.

surface.description: The store's own name for the endpoint, channel, report or field that provides it, verbatim enough for a reader to find the vendor page. Required whenever `available` is true, and forbidden when it is false: a surface on a false would qualify it in a form a validator accepts and a consumer ignores.

notes.description: Required whenever `available` is false, and wherever the surface carries a caveat an implementer would otherwise get wrong. A false MUST say which surfaces were examined.
